summary: Sketch relations now show on the canvas as small marks in the dimension colour, drawn as the same symbol that the Constrain menu and the relations list now show beside each relation. Horizontal or Vertical between a line's own ends sits beside the middle of that line, toward the inside of the sketch, and between points of different edges marks each point; Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear and Equal length mark each line; Equal radius and Point on curve mark the arc or circle, at the top of a circle or the middle of an arc; Coincident, Midpoint, Point on line and fixes mark their point; Symmetric marks both points and the axis; Tangent marks the joint. Fix X and Fix Y on one point share one Fixed mark while the relations list keeps both rows, and a Coincident relation between two arc or circle centers reads Concentric on the canvas, in the relations list, in constraint issues and in the status line. Several marks on one line or point sit side by side in screen pixels, in a fixed order, so they keep their size and spacing at every zoom. Dimensions keep their labels, and linear patterns and linked references keep their own controls, so they draw no mark. Marks lie beneath the sketch: where a mark covers a point, an edge, the origin, an axis, a profile grip or a profile edge, that geometry keeps the hover, click, right-click and drag. In Select, hovering a mark highlights the geometry its relation holds and the relation's other marks without rendering the sketch; hovering a relations or constraint issues row, or selecting geometry, highlights the marks of its relations. A click selects a mark's relation and replaces the geometry selection, Shift toggles and Escape clears; marks and canvas dimensions share one annotation selection and the status line names it, for example Parallel selected · Delete removes. Delete or Backspace removes the selected relations and dimensions in one undo step and keeps the geometry; a refused removal keeps the selection and shows its message. Double-click or Enter opens the relations list with the row active, and the right-click menu, the menu key and Shift+F10 offer Show in relations list and Delete on a relation mark, and Delete after the existing items on a dimension. Tab reaches the marks in Select, each named by its relation and operands, for example Parallel: Line 3 and Line 5; a mark that hides while focused returns focus to the canvas. With a drawing tool, during a pending Line chain or while a command picks geometry, marks take no pointer events or focus, and a drag keeps the pointer on what it moves. A sketch with more than 200 marks shows only those on selected or inspected geometry and the selected ones, and the status line says how many marks the sketch has. A new Show relations display setting, on by default, hides every mark and drops a selected one when turned off; the relations list and the Constrain tools work as before.
warning: Potentially breaking for automation and people that drive the sketch canvas: relation marks are new focusable canvas buttons, so Tab in Select now stops on each mark between the dimension labels and the points and edges, and automation that counts focus stops or tabs to a point must allow for them. They take a click where nothing else lies, so a click on empty canvas beside a mark that used to clear the selection now selects that relation; points, edges, the origin, axes and profile grips and edges beneath a mark keep their picks. Delete and Backspace now also remove selected relations: the canvas annotation selection, which held only dimensions, now holds relations and dimensions together, and cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty while a relation mark is selected or the relations list was opened from one, as it already was for a selected dimension. A Coincident relation between two arc or circle centers is now named Concentric in the relations list, constraint issues and status line, where it read Coincident; automation that finds a relations row by its label must use the new name. The dimension right-click menu ends with a separator and Delete, which counts every selected relation and dimension when the menu acts on a larger selection. WebMCP tools, their arguments and results, the CAD schema, the solver and saved documents are unchanged. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output.

checklist.schema: No CAD schema change: removals use the existing remove-sketch-relation edit through the same prepared batch as the relations list, and dimensions use the existing removal path. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol change; the Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. The new Show relations preference is a workbench display preference stored with the other CAD display settings, defaulting to on when absent, so older preference records load unchanged.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. The glyph layout is a pure function of the sketch graph, the view scale and the stacking order: operands come from cadSketchRelationPointIds and cadSketchRelationEntityIds through an exhaustive switch over relation kinds, offsets are screen pixels, and keys combine the relation ID, its kind and operands, so a reused ID never inherits a hover, selection or focus. Names, stacking slots and keys come from the sketch graph as last edited, which a drag preview does not replace, so a drag only places the shown marks again; above the mark limit only the shown entries are placed. The glyph layer is memoized and receives neither the cursor, the cursor pick, the snap candidate nor the view signature, and each row takes primitive props and a stable action object, so drawing-cursor moves, a rectangle readout and a pending Line chain render no glyph row. Hover lights operands and sibling marks through a highlight store that only the highlight overlay reads, so it renders no row and not the canvas. The layer is drawn after the dimension targets and before the point and edge rows, so the browser hit test gives geometry the pointer, and a mark press first asks the line cover and the 6 px geometry picker once per native event and declines without stopping propagation when either answers. Marks set pointer-events none and tabindex -1 unless the tool is Select with no pending path, pick or definition lock. A drag keeps the pointer captured by what it moves; during a drag or while an edit is applying, the layer takes no pointer events and the marks keep their tab stops, so starting or ending either renders no glyph row. Selections reuse the dimension annotation pick model, extended to every relation kind except linear patterns and linked references, and reconcile against the current graph after edits, undo and redo; CadSketchGraphSelection is unchanged. A removal of several relations and dimensions is one onEditMany batch and one undo step; a refused batch keeps the selection and shows its message. Show relations off drops non-dimension picks from the annotation selection in the same render. WebMCP tools and their arguments are unchanged; relation selection, like dimension selection, is not part of the agent viewport state, and docs/site/agents.md says that the selected geometry set is empty while a relation mark is selected.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. Sketch relations gain canvas marks with hover highlight, selection, Delete, double-click and Enter to open the relations list, a context menu and keyboard focus. The Constrain menu and the relations list show a relation icon. @wire-edm/icons-react gains 15 relation icons generated from scripts/icon-source.mjs; existing icons are unchanged. A Show relations display preference is added.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved documents open unchanged and older releases open documents edited with this one; the new preference is ignored by older releases.
checklist.verification:
New tests:
- cadSketchRelationGlyphLayout.test.ts: placement for every relation kind, stacking order and spacing in screen pixels, the shared Fixed mark, Concentric naming, relations that draw no mark, broken relations, and new mount keys for reused IDs.
- CadSketchCanvasRender.test.tsx: drawing-cursor moves, hover, a pending Line chain, and starting or ending a drag render no glyph row. Above the 200-mark limit, only marks on selected geometry and selected marks are drawn, and the status line says so in Select only.
- CadWorkbench.test.tsx: select, Shift, Escape, Delete in one undo step, refused removal, double-click and Enter to the relations list, the context menu, list-row and selection highlighting, accessible names, no pointer events or focus with a drawing tool, a pending Line chain or a geometry pick, and the Show relations setting.
- cadSketchDimensionSelection, CadSketchRelationsPanel and CadSettingsPanel tests were extended.
- e2e/cad-sketch-relation-glyphs.spec.ts in Chromium: hover, select, Delete and Undo, double-click to the list; marks follow a dragged edge during and after the drag; a click beside a mark keeps the geometry pick; with Line, marks are inert while a chain is pending.

Checks:
- Full Vitest: 557 files, 6468 tests passed.
- npm run build, npm run lint (zero findings), npm run ui:check and npm run icons:check pass, as does node scripts/check-release.mjs without a base.
- Chromium specs, run one at a time with two workers, all passed (45 tests): cad-sketch-relation-glyphs, cad-sketch-constraints, cad-sketch-dimension-selection, cad-sketch-arc-trim, cad-sketch-editing, cad-sketch-context-editing, cad-sketch-selectable-axes, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions, cad-sketch-line-chain, cad-sketch-point-on-line, cad-sketch-profile-copy and cad-sketch-circle-trim.

Measurements:
- Setup: Chromium at 4x CPU slowdown, branch and main 0.0.781 production builds run alternately, medians of 4 runs.
- Sketch: grids of 10 mm rectangles with Horizontal and Vertical on every edge.
- 200 marks shown:
  - A 60-move point drag took 6.7 s against 5.4 s, with long tasks 2.7 s against 1.6 s.
  - Hover handled P50 was 29 ms against 24 ms in Select, and 30 ms against 24 ms with Rectangle.
- 400 marks shown, with the limit raised for the measurement only: the drag took 9.6 s against 6.8 s, with long tasks 6.8 s against 3.8 s.
- 400 relations above the limit, none shown: the drag took 6.7 s against 6.6 s, and hover handled P50 was 27 ms against 28 ms.
- The limit of 200 is therefore kept.

Out of scope: no controller or machine verification applies, because output is unchanged.

publicNotes.summary: Sketch relations show as marks on the canvas that you can select and delete.
changes: Each sketch relation draws a small mark on the canvas beside the geometry it holds, with the same symbol the Constrain menu and the relations list now show.
Hover a mark to highlight the geometry its relation holds; hovering a relations or issue row, or selecting geometry, highlights the marks of its relations.
Click a mark to select its relation, Shift-click to add or remove one and Escape to clear. Delete or Backspace removes the selected relations and dimensions in one undo step.
Double-click a mark, or press Enter on it, to open the relations list on its row. Right-click it for Show in relations list and Delete.
Fix X and Fix Y on one point show as one Fixed mark, and a Coincident relation between two centers reads Concentric.
Marks never take a click from the geometry under them, and they ignore the pointer while you draw, during a Line chain or while a command picks geometry.
Settings → CAD → Display → Show relations hides the marks; the relations list and the Constrain tools keep working.
publicNotes.compatibility: Sketches keep using existing relation kinds, so earlier releases open them. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: Tab in the sketch now stops on relation marks, and a click on a mark beside the geometry selects that relation; turn off Settings → CAD → Display → Show relations to hide them. Automation that finds a relations row named Coincident between two centers should use Concentric.
